Per-day caps do most of the work. Daily values are 0 to 3, so a day totals at most 12.

Pesmisto: total 5, maximum 2 only once, so its days are 2, 0, 1, 1, 1 in some order. Kitmisto: total 14 with a maximum of 3 a day, so four 3s and one 2. On Day 2 Kitmisto has 3 and nobody else does, so Levmisto, Tyhrmisto, Pesmisto are at most 2.

2022-3-s35:
Introduce unknowns from the ratios. Let CS students = c. Non-CS students take exactly one course, and total c as well; with ratio 2 : 5 they are 2k in AI and 5k in ML, so 7k = c.

CS grades: AI (nobody fails) A : B : C = 3 : 5 : 2, so c = 10n. ML: A : B : C = 4 : 5 : 2 among passes, so passes = 11m and CS failures x = c − 11m.

Let f be the number of non-CS failures in each course. Fact 3: 2f = CS C grades in ML = 2m, so f = m. Fact 7: 2f = 3x, so x = 2m/3. Fact 8: f + x = 30 gives m = 18, x = 12, f = 18. So c = 11 × 18 + 12 = 210, k = 30, n = 21.

Now the grades. AI: 210 CS + 60 non-CS = 270 students; 18 fail, 252 pass; B is half = 126, A = C = 63. ML: 210 + 150 = 360 students; 30 fail, 330 pass; B = 165, A = 99, C = 66.
